summary.text: A 9-year-old Korean boy was found to have microscopic hematuria at a school check-up, was suspected at another hospital of acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, and had consistently low complement levels. At his outpatient visit on November 30, 2018, C3 was 24.4 mg/dL with normal C4, urinalysis showed microscopic hematuria without proteinuria, and kidney ultrasonography showed no remarkable findings. He developed proteinuria in July 2019.

The parents refused a renal biopsy and genetic study, so prednisolone was prescribed and later tapered for gastrointestinal side effects. Losartan was started and adjusted, and cyclosporine was started, stopped after cognitive decline, dizziness and depression, and later re-introduced. C3 stayed very low, and he was hospitalized on June 9, 2021 with weight loss, vomiting, abdominal pain and increased proteinuria, and was diagnosed with pancreatitis.

Next-generation sequencing on August 18, 2021 showed a heterozygous likely pathogenic C3 frameshift variant plus PKD1, FBN2 and MFAP5 variants. A kidney biopsy on June 30, 2022 showed C3GN with diffuse proliferative features, and he was diagnosed with C3GN and C3 deficiency without recurrent bacterial infections. Specialist consultations found no other abnormalities, and he was vaccinated against pneumococcus.

Mycophenolate mofetil was started on June 12, 2021 and later reduced for skin rash and gastric and duodenal ulcers, and losartan and cyclosporine were adjusted through November 2022. Currently kidney function is normal, but proteinuria and hematuria persist. The father and older brother share the C3 mutation, the older brother has low C3 and hematuria, and follow-up is continuing.
